parsed.rationale: Sinus rhythm with QS complexes in V1–V3 and Q waves into V4, plus deep T-wave inversions in V3–V5; ST elevation is only about 1 mm in V2 and minimal in V1/V3, below the STEMI threshold for V2–V3 (≥1.5–2.5 mm by sex/age), so it looks like an evolved or older anterior infarct rather than an acute STEMI and should be read alongside symptoms, troponin and old ECGs.
